title: Handley Page Halifax LK794
memorial_details:
Brushed stainless steel engraved plaque on oak stand.

IWM records the plaque as brushed stainless steel on an oak stand, unveiled on 18 July 1998, with the 578 Burn Association responsible for it.
inscription: ON THE MORNING OF 18 JULY 1944, 21 HALIFAX MK BIII/ BOMBERS OF 578 SQUADRON ROYAL AIR FORCE TOOK OFF/ FROM BURN IN NORTH YORKSHIRE TO ATTACK FORTIFIED/ VILLAGES NEAR CAEN IN FRANCE. ON THE OUTWARD FLIGHT/ LK-Q DEVELOPED A FIRE WHICH THE CREW WERE UNABLE/ TO CONTROL. THE PILOT MANAGED TO AVOID THE HEAVILY/ POPULATED AREAS OF READING AND MAIDENHEAD BEFORE/ THE AIRCRAFT EXPLODED AND PLUNGED INTO THIS WOOD./ MIRACULOUSLY THE CANADIAN REAR GUNNER MANAGED TO/ PARACHUTE TO SAFETY BUT THE REST OF THE CREW WERE LOST/ WITHOUT TRACE. THEIR NAMES, WHICH ARE RECORDED AT/ THE RAF MEMORIAL TO THE MISSING AT RUNNYMEDE ARE/ (Names)/ TREAD SOFTLY HERE FOR THIS IS HALLOWED GROUND

sources.title: Lest We Forget: Flying Officer Victor Starkoff DFC

narrative:
On the morning of 18 July 1944, 21 Halifax III bombers of 578 Squadron took off from Burn in North Yorkshire to attack fortified villages near Caen. One of them, coded LK-Q, caught fire on the outward flight and the crew could not put it out. The plaque says the pilot steered clear of Reading and Maidenhead before the aircraft exploded and fell into the wood where the memorial now stands.

Six of the seven crew died. The Canadian rear gunner baled out and survived; the plaque says the others were lost without trace and are named on the Runnymede Memorial. The six names on the stone are the pilot, Flying Officer Victor Starkoff DFC of the RAAF, aged 33; navigator Pilot Officer Jan Fink, 26; wireless operator Pilot Officer Lloyde Hopper of the RCAF; air bomber Flight Sergeant Ivor Morgan, 20; flight engineer Sergeant Gerald Nicholson, 20, from Liverpool; and mid-upper gunner Flight Sergeant John Claque. An Australian museum page, which appears to copy the Australian War Memorial, names the surviving rear gunner as Flight Sergeant H C Sloan, RCAF.

Sources disagree on the serial. The IWM register and the IBCC losses database give LK794; the Australian museum page and Traces of War give LK974. Our record's LK794 follows the two institutional sources. The same museum page puts the crash at Bisham, while IWM places the memorial at Carpenters Wood, Burchetts Green; the two places are near each other.

external_narratives.summary: Our capture of the IWM record. Gives the plaque inscription (578 Squadron, Burn to Caen, LK-Q fire, Canadian rear gunner baled out, six lost and commemorated at Runnymede), six names, location at Carpenters Wood off Dungrove Hill Lane, and two photos by Paul Clarke. Web search summaries of the live page add that the plaque was unveiled on 18 July 1998 and that the 578 Burn Association is responsible; the capture's History/Commemoration sections were empty.

Reproduces Australian War Memorial roll-of-honour style text for Starkoff and lists the whole seven-man crew with ranks, service numbers, air forces, roles and fate. Names the aircraft as Halifax LK974, takeoff from Burn 0520 for Caen, starboard engine fire at 8,000 ft and a crash at Bisham, Berkshire. The text appears to derive from the AWM (service number page awm.gov.au/collection/P10317700), so it may not be independent of the AWM.

Staff memorial page for Sgt Gerald Thomas Nicholson RAFVR, born Liverpool 10 December 1923, died aged 20. Describes the 18 July 1944 flight from Burn: engine fire, pilot steering clear of populated areas, mid-air explosion, six of seven killed.
